elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause retains automatic renewal ("will renew automatically for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term") and no mutual-written-agreement gate is added; the conditional automatic-renewal elements are not all satisfied (no 12-month cap on the renewal term, 60-day rather than 30-day opt-out, no Vendor reminder), so the preferred pathway is not opened.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Renewal is for "an additional term equal in duration to the previous term of the applicable Service Option Attachment" — the length is whatever the Attachment term was, with no express 12-month ceiling; a multi-year Attachment would auto-renew for multiple years. Fix: insert "but in no event longer than twelve (12) months".

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Operative text requires notice "at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term"; 60 > 30. Fix: substitute thirty (30) days for the preferred level.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder obligation appears anywhere in the rendered language; it is only mentioned in the margin comment as the unpressed preferred position, which is not operative.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: §3.2 as rendered contains no uplift mechanic — renewal is simply for an additional term of equal duration, with no repricing right embedded in the renewal clause. The separate unilateral price-change right in §13.1 (available only after 12 months, on 90 days' notice, with a fee-free exit) is a change-of-terms mechanic outside the renewal provision.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Rendered: "unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term" — the window is exactly 60 days, at the fallback ceiling. The deterministic check reporting "number not found" is a matcher artefact; the operative text plainly reads sixty (60).

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the renewal clause grants no repricing right (renewal is for an equal-duration term with no fee escalation language), so no cap is required here.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the 60-day non-renewal window is met on the face of the rendered text, and the price-cap element is inapplicable because §3.2 contains no renewal uplift mechanic.

Preferred level fails on four elements: no mutual-agreement gate, no 12-month cap on the renewal term (renewal tracks the previous term's duration, so a multi-year Attachment auto-renews multi-year), a 60-day rather than 30-day opt-out, and no 60-day Vendor renewal reminder. To reach preferred the drafter must (a) change sixty (60) to thirty (30), (b) add "but in no event longer than twelve (12) months" to the renewal term, and (c) add an express Vendor obligation to notify Customer at least 60 days before each renewal.

Minimality holds: the edit is a single numeric substitution (ninety (90) → sixty (60)); the mutual either-party right, writing requirement, per-Attachment structure and term-end anchor are retained verbatim, with no extras, survival tails or added procedures.

Intent preserved: no defined term, cross-reference or commercial mechanic is disturbed; the §13.1 price-change right (a change-of-terms mechanic, correctly not double-flagged under RENEWAL) is untouched and does not contradict the amended §3.2.

Residual watch-item for the drafter: because the renewal term simply mirrors the prior term, a Service Option Attachment with a term longer than 12 months would produce an automatic multi-year renewal, which is walk-away territory under this rule — confirm Attachment terms or add the 12-month cap.
